concern.concern: The Statement instructs: “cut B⁴ along a thickened copy of the pushed-in surface” and “do not glue the last positive face to the first negative face,” then calls the result the cyclic branched cover. Proof 3.1 nevertheless asserts that the cut sheets form the local model w↦w^q and that a meridian moves cyclically through all q sheets. Taken literally as cut-face gluing, the specified chain leaves terminal faces unmatched and does not establish that local branched-cover model. A pushed-in surface also has codimension two, so the cutting hypersurface and its faces require specification. The standard q−1 interfaces in a handle or thickened-surface construction must be distinguished from q cyclic cut-face identifications. Proof 1.1 assumes the cut pieces are 4-balls and obtains the handles without supplying this distinction; the chain diagram does not resolve it. The matrix itself is corroborated by Przytycki–Yasuhara §3, printed p. 13 (https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/0111203), which attributes the surgery construction to Akbulut–Kirby. I could not extract a readable argument from the retrieved Akbulut–Kirby PDF, so I do not claim to have checked that original construction. The literal construction and its claimed boundary remain unsupported as written.

required_own_edits.source_excerpt: Push the interior of $F$ into $B^4$ while keeping $K$ on $S^3=\partial B^4$, cut $B^4$ along a thickened copy of the pushed-in surface, and take $q$ copies. For $i=1,\ldots,q-1$, glue the positive face of copy $i$ to the negative face of copy $i+1$ by reflecting the normal coordinate; do not glue the last positive face to the first negative face. Call the resulting $q$-fold cyclic branched cover $W_q(F)$. It has one $0$-handle and $2g(q-1)$ $2$-handles, and its framed attaching link has linking matrix $M_q(V)$. The boundary branched cover, with the boundary marking induced by the covering map, is $\Sigma_q(K)$.
required_own_edits.proposed_replacement: Push the interior of $F$ into $B^4$ while keeping $K$ on $S^3=\partial B^4$, and let $W_q(F)$ be the actual $q$-fold cyclic branched cover along that pushed-in surface. Use the following disk-band handle model of this cover. Cut $B^4$ along the three-dimensional track of the push-in isotopy; the cut-open manifold is again a $4$-ball and its boundary contains the thickened surface $\bar F=(F\times[-1,1])/\sim$, where $(x,t)\sim(x,t')$ for $x\in\partial F$. Write $\bar F^\pm=\{(x,t)\in\bar F:\pm t\ge0\}$. Take $q$ copies of this cut-open ball and, for $i=1,\ldots,q-1$, glue $\bar F_i^+$ to $\bar F_{i+1}^-$ by $(x,t)\mapsto(x,-t)$. The Akbulut–Kirby construction identifies this handle model with $W_q(F)$; the last-to-first gluing is unnecessary for the underlying manifold in this model. This is a statement about the isotopy-track handle model, not an assertion that an open chain of normal-disk sectors is already the cyclic covering map. The resulting handle presentation has one $0$-handle and $2g(q-1)$ $2$-handles, and its framed attaching link has linking matrix $M_q(V)$. The boundary branched cover, with the boundary marking induced by the covering map of $W_q(F)$, is $\Sigma_q(K)$.

required_own_edits.source_excerpt: [F4] The $q$-fold branched cover of $S^3$ is formed from the meridian-mod-$q$ cover of the compact exterior by filling the lift of $\mu^q$. [[def-cyclic-branched-cover-of-a-knot]]
required_own_edits.proposed_replacement:
[F4] The $q$-fold branched cover of $S^3$ is formed from the meridian-mod-$q$ cover of the compact exterior by filling the lift of $\mu^q$. [[def-cyclic-branched-cover-of-a-knot]]

[F5] **External input (Akbulut–Kirby disk-band construction).** For a connected oriented Seifert surface in $S^3$, pushed into $B^4$, the $q$-fold cyclic branched cover is represented by cutting along the push-in isotopy track and gluing $q$ cut-open balls along the thickened half-surfaces as specified above, using only the $q-1$ adjacent-copy gluings. The terminal gluing is unnecessary for the underlying manifold. If the surface has one disk and $b$ bands, the disk gluings give one $0$-handle; each band gives one $2$-handle at each of the $q-1$ layers, with attaching circle obtained from the two corresponding face-core arcs and with the carried band framing. The actual branched covering map restricts on the boundary to the cyclic cover branched along the boundary link. This is the explicitly imported construction of Akbulut–Kirby, §2, printed pp.113–114 and the boundary-restriction Remark p.116; the paper's smooth oriented conventions are on p.111. It is not claimed as a locally reconstructed handle-identification proof. [Akbulut–Kirby, *Branched Covers of Surfaces in 4-Manifolds*, Math. Ann.252 (1980),111–131](https://math.berkeley.edu/~kirby/papers/Akbulut%20and%20Kirby%20-%20Branched%20covers%20of%20surfaces%20in%204-manifolds%20-%20MR0593626.pdf).

required_own_edits.source_excerpt: 1.1 By [F1] and [F2], cut $B^4$ along the thickening of the pushed-in disk-band surface, producing cut copies $B_1^4,\ldots,B_q^4$. First glue these copies only along the disk $0$-handle of the branch surface. A disk thickening is a $3$-ball in the boundary of each cut $4$-ball; joining the two face balls for consecutive copies is the standard boundary-connected-sum operation, so the resulting $4$-manifold is again a $4$-ball with one $0$-handle. For each surface band, the positive face of copy $k$ glued to the negative face of copy $k+1$ joins the two band-core arcs; its regular neighborhood is a $2$-handle $D^2\times D^2$ attached along $S^1\times D^2$. There are $q-1$ such seams and $2g$ bands, so the construction gives $2g(q-1)$ $2$-handles and no other handles. [A1, F1, F2, given, construct]
required_own_edits.proposed_replacement: 1.1 Use the isotopy-track handle model supplied by [F5], not a cut of the codimension-two branch surface itself. By [F1] and [F2], the connected surface has one disk and $2g$ bands. In the model, the disk-face gluings combine the $q$ cut-open $4$-balls into a $4$-ball with one $0$-handle. The remaining face gluings give, for each band and each adjacent-copy layer $k=1,\ldots,q-1$, a $2$-handle whose attaching circle joins that band's two face-core arcs through the common disk region, with the carried band framing. Hence there are $2g(q-1)$ $2$-handles and no other handles. The identification of this model with the actual cyclic branched cover, including the legitimacy of omitting the terminal gluing, is the external input [F5]; the local linking-entry computation below uses its attaching-circle description. [A1, F1, F2, F5, given, construct]

required_own_edits.source_excerpt: 3.1 In a normal disk to the branch surface, the $q$ cut sheets form the standard cyclic degree-$q$ branched disk; its map is $w\mapsto w^q$. Away from the branch locus, a positive meridian moves through the $q$ sheets cyclically, so the boundary exterior cover is the connected cover classified by the homomorphism $\pi_1(E_K)\to\mathbb Z/q$ sending $\mu$ to $1$. Its meridian boundary is the closed lift of $\mu^q$, which bounds the filling disk. By [F4] and uniqueness of the classified connected cover, the boundary with its branch marking is $\Sigma_q(K)$. [F4, step 1.1, step 2.1, given]
required_own_edits.proposed_replacement: 3.1 Apply the branched covering map on the actual cover $W_q(F)$ identified with the handle model by [F5]. Its normal-disk map is $w\mapsto w^q$; this is not a claim about the unmatched terminal banks of the handle model. A positive meridian away from the branch locus moves cyclically through the $q$ sheets. Restriction to the boundary therefore gives the connected exterior cover classified by $\pi_1(E_K)\to\mathbb Z/q$, $\mu\mapsto1$, and the lift of $\mu^q$ bounds the normal filling disk. This is exactly the boundary restriction in [F5] and the exterior/filling definition [F4]. Thus the boundary with the marking induced by the actual branched covering map is $\Sigma_q(K)$. No canonical covering map on the unclosed raw handle model is being asserted. [F4, F5, step 1.1, given]
